title: Triads in progressions and improvisation
description: Comping, outlining, and chord-tone melody from the same triad tones.

cards.front: What three jobs can a triad do in a progression?
cards.back: Comping (short upper-string voicings over a bass). Outlining (arpeggio so a line states the harmony). Improvising (triad tones as strong targets, scale notes as connections).

cards.front: Which notes agree with the chord at any moment?
cards.back: Root, third, and fifth. Other scale notes pass between them.

cards.front: Where should chord tones vs passing notes sit?
cards.back: Strong beats hold chord tones; weak beats hold passing notes. Reverse that and the line sounds like it ignores the chords.

cards.front: Why is the third the most informative chord tone?
cards.back: It decides major or minor. Landing on the third of each chord makes the changes audible.

cards.front: List triad tones of G Em C D (I vi IV V in G).
cards.back: G B D, E G B, C E G, D F♯ A.

cards.front: In G–Em–C–D, which notes are shared with the next chord?
cards.back: G to Em: G B. Em to C: E G. C to D: none. D to G: D. Only D contains F♯, the leading tone.

cards.front: What is an approach tone vs a passing tone?
cards.back: Approach: a half step below or above a target, leading into it (F♯ or A into G). Passing: a scale tone between two chord tones on a weak beat (C between B and D).

cards.front: What four pitch classes do you get from an Em triad over a C bass? What color is that?
cards.back: C E G B — a major-seventh color (Cmaj7). The triad’s meaning changes with the bass under it.

cards.front: Give the smooth G–Em–C–D–G path on strings 3–2–1.
cards.back: G 7 8 7 (D G B). Em 9 8 7 (E G B). C 9 8 8 (E G C). D 7 7 5 (D F♯ A). Back to 7 8 7. Motion 2, 1, 6, 3. Frets 5–9.

cards.front: Where are the bass roots for G Em C D on the lower strings?
cards.back: G string 6 fret 3. Em string 6 open. C string 5 fret 3. D string 4 open.

cards.front: Give the 4/4 eighths comping pattern, one chord per bar.
cards.back: Beat 1: bass root alone. And-of-2: short triad. Beat 3: bass root or its fifth. And-of-4: triad again.

cards.front: Quarter-note outline of G Em C D on 3–2–1 (note names).
cards.back: G: D G B G. Em: E G B G. C: E G C G. D: D F♯ A F♯. G holds across the first three bars, then moves to F♯.

cards.front: What are the three improvisation steps over the same four chords?
cards.back: 1. Chord tones only; land on the third on beat 1 (B, G, E, F♯). 2. Add G-major passing tones on weak beats. 3. Add a half-step approach on the beat before the target.

cards.front: Why avoid holding C over a G chord?
cards.back: C sits a half step above the chord’s B, so it clashes if you stay on it. Fine as a short passing tone; over the C chord it is the root.

cards.front: List triad tones of Am F C G.
cards.back: A C E, F A C, C E G, G B D.

cards.front: C–Am–F–G on 4–3–2 with added bass roots. Give frets and bass locations.
cards.back: Shapes 10 9 8, 10 9 10, 10 10 10, 9 7 8. Bass: C string 5 fret 3; A string 5 open; F string 6 fret 1; G string 6 fret 3.
